reasoning_notes.reasoning: Any positive wage loses to a lower bid or earns less when matched; at zero, a tie yields half the labor at zero cost.
With no history, a middle wage balances the chance of winning labor against margin; it also leaves room to adjust later.
Undercut C’s last wage of 10 to win the unit at a positive margin.
A earned nothing at 0 while I captured the unit at 10. Repeating 10 preserves a profitable offer and may reveal whether A adapts.
C has bid 10 twice; matching 10 yields half the labor and profit 5, while bidding higher risks a loss and undercutting earns less per unit.
Both firms earn 10 at a tie on 10. A bid above 10 wins all labor but earns less per unit; bidding below risks losing the round. Repeat 10.

C has bid 10 in every round. Matching 10 earns half the labor and 5 profit; undercutting by 1 would win all labor for 11 profit, but risks a lower wage if C changes its bid. Given the repeated bid, match at 10.

Undercutting A’s repeated 10 captures the full unit and earns 11, improving on the 5 from matching. A may respond in later rounds, but this round’s gain is clear.
